=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:476-483 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A bare `HEAD` refspec is treated as a literal destination branch, so the guard checks GitHub for branch `HEAD` instead of the current branch.
  WHY: That lookup finds no matching PR and can allow a push from a merged branch; severity disagreement: five reviewers rated this BLOCKER and openai_gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:447-468 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Refspec extraction assumes the first positional is the remote even when `--repo` consumed the remote or no positional remote was provided, dropping the first refspec.
  WHY: The guard then checks the current branch rather than the destination and can allow a push to a merged destination; severity disagreement: google_gemini-3_8-flash and qwen_qwen3_7-plus rated this BLOCKER while the other reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:256-264,458-483 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: File-descriptor redirection digits can be parsed as refspecs, causing an invalid source lookup and fallback to checking the session checkout.
  WHY: A valid worktree push can be falsely blocked based on the unrelated checkout; severity disagreement: google_gemini-3_8-flash rated this BLOCKER while the other reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:461-483 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Uncertain push-option or refspec fallbacks use the session checkout as `cwd` instead of the already-resolved `invocation.cwd`.
  WHY: The guard can check the wrong branch for a push from a worktree, causing either a missed block or a false block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:322-323 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `||` operator clears the parser's resolved working directory even though a successful preceding `cd` leaves the shell in that directory.
  WHY: A later push may be checked against the session checkout rather than the worktree, causing a missed block or false block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:337-348 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The leading-assignment recognizer accepts `NAME=value` but not Bash `NAME+=value`, so the guarded Git invocation can go unrecognized.
  WHY: `_evaluate_bash` may return without checking the push destination; severity disagreement: minimax_minimax-m3 rated this BLOCKER while the other reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:479-482 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Source validation rejects valid Git revisions containing characters such as `~`, `^`, or `@`, causing the fallback to discard the parsed destination.
  WHY: The fallback can check the session checkout instead of the worktree and destination branch, allowing a push without checking the target PR status.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1313-1351 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A single Bash command can emit multiple hook JSON responses when GitHub is unreachable, including across multiple targets or a bulk-push confirmation.
  WHY: The hook harness expects a single JSON payload, so multiple JSON lines can break response parsing or tool gating.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:328-331 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: After the working directory becomes unknown, the `cd` handler cannot resolve a subsequent absolute path because it requires `working_directory` to be non-None.
  WHY: The guard can remain uncertain and check the session checkout instead of the explicitly named worktree.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:256-360 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A leading shell redirection can make the segment start with a filename rather than `git`, so the Git push invocation is not recorded.
  WHY: The push then receives no guard evaluation and can proceed without checking its destination branch.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:246-483,1262-1353 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The workflow-template twin contains the same flawed parser and evaluation logic as the root hook.
  WHY: Consumer repositories receiving the template can inherit the reported missed-block and false-block defects.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Acceptance criteria require regression tests for the bare `git push origin HEAD` case.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: google_gemini-3_8-flash: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py only tests explicit refspecs of the form HEAD:<open-PR branch> and lacks a bare-HEAD regression test; z-ai_glm-5_2: no test covers bare `git push origin HEAD`.
- requirement: Acceptance criteria require tests covering `git push --repo origin ...`, redirection syntax such as `2>&1`, chained command structures such as `cd worktree || exit 1`, and append-assignment prefixes such as `VAR+=val git push`.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  EVIDENCE: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py only tests explicit refspecs of the form HEAD:<open-PR branch>; it lacks regression tests for option-specified remotes, redirection syntax, chained command structures, and append-assignment prefixes.
- requirement: "If the directory cannot be resolved (a variable, a subshell), keep today's behaviour for that command and log a warning. Don't fail open silently."
  expected_change_site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: No test covers a resolved worktree with an uncertain refspec.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _push_targets lines 476-483 (bare refspec without colon sets source=destination=refspec, then _branch_ref returns the literal string); _branch_ref in PR diff; _evaluate_bash branch = target.branch or current_branch(target.cwd)
  severity=critical confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Bare `HEAD` is used as the branch to check instead of resolving the current branch, so a push from a merged branch can pass the guard.
  WHY: The GitHub lookup for branch `HEAD` finds no matching PR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _shell_segments_with_operators token splitting with punctuation_chars=_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS where > is punctuation; _push_targets positionals collecting; _evaluate_bash source tip fallback to checkout
  severity=high confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The `2` in `2>&1` can be parsed as a refspec, whose failed source lookup falls back to the session checkout.
  WHY: A valid worktree push can be falsely blocked based on the checkout's branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _guarded_git_invocations operator check "if operator not in ("", "&&", ";", "\n"): working_directory = None" for "||" operator
  severity=high confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The `||` operator clears the directory resolved by a preceding `cd`.
  WHY: A subsequent push is checked against the session checkout instead of the worktree.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _guarded_git_invocations leading-assignment loop — re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=", tokens[index]) does not match Bash NAME+=value syntax
  severity=high confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: A Bash `NAME+=value` prefix prevents the Git push from being recognized.
  WHY: The invocation is skipped and the push destination is not checked.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _push_targets source validation — re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+|HEAD", source) rejects valid revisions like HEAD~1, HEAD@{u}, feature/x
  severity=high confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Valid Git source revisions are rejected, causing fallback that discards the parsed destination.
  WHY: The guard can check the session checkout rather than the push destination.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _evaluate_bash multi-target loop — _unreachable_outcome called for each target whose API query failed, which calls _request_confirmation for pushes
  severity=high confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Multiple unreachable push targets can each emit a hook JSON response.
  WHY: The hook harness expects a single JSON payload.
- TASK COMPLETENESS (reported no gap)
  Requirement: "Acceptance: tests in tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py cover all of these: a cd <worktree> && git push origin HEAD:<open-PR branch> from a main checkout sitting on a merged branch is allowed; a push to a merged branch with no open PR is blocked, whatever the main checkout is on; git -C <path> behaves the same way; an unresolvable directory falls back to today's behaviour."
  Expected change site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Evidence of absence: The four bullet points from the acceptance criteria are all covered by the new tests. No gap exists against the explicit acceptance criteria.
  severity=low confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The reviewer reports the stated acceptance criteria are covered and identifies no gap against them.
